summary: Feed s162_triple to IDS is degraded: 50% of packets missing required VLAN 20, 5.3% jumbo frames (up to 8104B) dropped by 1518B IDS port, and 27.7% VXLAN-encapsulated traffic opaque to IDS.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is stripping 802.1Q tags or VLAN 20 is pruned/filtered before the tool port; 50% of packets arrive untagged and VLAN 20 is never seen despite being required.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS has no visibility into VLAN 20 - misses half the traffic, breaks VLAN-based detection/policy and creates blind spot for lateral movement on VLAN 20.

recommended_fix.why: IDS requires VLANs 10 and 20 for correct classification; broker must preserve/restore 802.1Q tags for VLAN 20 on egress to tool.

findings.root_cause: Network/broker delivering jumbo/VXLAN-encapsulated frames up to 8104 bytes to a 1Gbps IDS port limited to 1518 bytes. Broker is not handling MTU mismatch and IDS NIC drops oversize frames.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS NIC silently drops 5.3% (114/2141) of frames that exceed 1518B, so IDS never inspects them. Because IDS needs full payload for signature matching, payload trimming/slicing is not viable and those flows are missed.

recommended_fix.why: Tool needs full payload so slicing would break detection; fix is to enable jumbo frames/increase MTU on IDS port/NIC or reduce MTU upstream, not slice.

findings.root_cause: 27.7% of traffic (593/2141) is VXLAN-encapsulated and packet broker is forwarding outer tunnel headers without stripping. Likely VXLAN overlay from virtualized/DC fabric passed straight to tool.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS sees only outer VXLAN/IP/UDP headers, not inner Ethernet/IP payload, so it cannot apply signatures or detect threats inside 27.7% of traffic.

recommended_fix.why: Stripping VXLAN at the packet broker exposes inner packets for IDS inspection, restoring detection coverage for overlay traffic.
